title: Geometry - Lesson 1 Assessment: Explaining Circle Area
description: Show that you can describe how cutting and rearranging circle sectors forms the circle area formula.

questions.question: A circle is cut into equal sectors and rearranged point-up and point-down. What known shape does the arrangement begin to resemble?
questions.explanation: The alternating sectors form an almost rectangle, especially when many thin sectors are used.

questions.question: The area formula for a circle can be connected to the rectangle formula area = base × height.
questions.explanation: The rearranged sectors form an almost rectangle, so base times height helps explain circle area.

questions.question: Why is the base of the rearranged sector model about πr?
options: It is half of the circumference 2πr.
It is the same as the diameter.
It is twice the radius plus 1.
questions.explanation: One long bumpy side uses about half of the circle's curved edge. Half of 2πr is πr.

questions.question: Complete the formula formed by the rearranged sector model: (πr)(r) = ______.
questions.correctAnswer: πr^2 or pi r^2 or πr² or pi r squared
questions.explanation: Multiplying pi r by r gives pi r squared.

questions.question: A circle has radius 5 cm. Which expression represents its area?
If a circle's diameter is given, you should use the diameter directly as r in A = πr².
questions.explanation: The formula uses radius. If diameter is given, divide it by 2 first.

questions.question: A circle has diameter 20 cm. Its radius is ______ cm.
questions.explanation: Radius is half the diameter. Half of 20 is 10.

questions.question: A student says, 'The rearranged base is 2πr, so the area is 2πr².' Correct the student's reasoning.
questions.correctAnswer: The student used the whole circumference as one base. In the rearranged sectors, one long side is about half the circumference, so the base is pi r and the area is (pi r)(r) = pi r squared.
questions.explanation: The correction must identify half circumference, not full circumference, as the base.

questions.question: In two or three sentences, describe how cutting and rearranging circle sectors helps form the area formula.
questions.correctAnswer: Cutting the circle into sectors and rearranging them does not change the area. The pieces make an almost rectangle with height r and base about pi r, so area = base times height becomes (pi r)(r) = pi r squared.
questions.explanation: A complete answer mentions preserved area, almost rectangle, base pi r, height r, and the formula.

questions.question: Which statement best explains why the sector model is an estimate that becomes exact as the number of sectors increases?
options: More sectors make the rearranged shape closer to a true rectangle.
More sectors make the circle's radius larger.
More sectors change π into a whole number.
More sectors remove the curved boundary from the circle.
questions.explanation: More, thinner sectors reduce the bumpiness of the rearranged shape, making the rectangle model more accurate.
